reauth_confirm.description: The server rejected the API token. Enter a new one.

data.charging_refresh_interval: Ask the car for data every N minutes while charging
data.track_location: Show the car on the map (device tracker)
data.idle_refresh_interval: Check on the parked car every N hours/days
data.driving_check_interval: Ask a car that seems to be driving every N minutes

data_description.charging_refresh_interval: Sends the "Refresh data" command only while the car's last known state is charging. Off by default.
data_description.data_fresh_minutes: Used by the "Data Fresh" binary sensor.
data_description.use_websocket: The server pushes changes as they happen. The update interval then acts only as a backup read in case the live connection stops working (30 minutes or the interval, whichever is longer). Turn off if your network blocks WebSockets.
data_description.track_location: On: a device tracker entity shows the car on the map. Off: no tracker is created and the position is left out of the Status sensor attributes.
data_description.idle_refresh_interval: Sends "Refresh data" to the car when it has been silent this long and is neither charging nor driving. Each command wakes the car's modem (12 V battery), so use a long interval; after a timeout it waits a full interval before trying again. Off by default.
data_description.driving_check_interval: Sends "Refresh data" while the car reports driving, until it answers that it is parked (the server only clears "driving" when the car sends a packet with the ignition off, which does not happen when the end-of-trip report is declined on the navigation screen). After 3 unanswered questions in a row it pauses until the car sends data, to protect the 12 V battery. Off by default.

confirm.title: Reconnect live updates
confirm.description: The live connection to OpenCARWINGS has been down for more than 10 minutes. Data is still read from the server periodically, but changes arrive late. Select Submit to reconnect now.
